GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The TUI is a separate client process in OpenCode v2 and loads client-side plugin modules from the plugins array of the global cli.json, not from opencode.json. Host source (packages/cli/src/config/migrate.ts) migrates the retired V1 tui.json plugin list into cli.json on first v2 start, so every machine upgraded from V1 carries a second vvoc pin that only the host ever wrote. The vvoc v2 config layer modeled a single pin in opencode.json, so install, sync, upgrade, status, and doctor were blind to the client pin; the observed incident was a server on 2.1.5 with a TUI fossilized on 2.1.2 that lacked /vv-rebind while vvoc upgrade reported success. The fix mirrors the proven opencode.json pin flow onto cli.json with the same managed-entry normalization and comment-preserving editor, and teaches the inspectors to show and compare both pins.

Alternatives.Alternative: Do nothing and document that users must edit cli.json manually after upgrades. Rejected: the drift is created by the host migration, is invisible to every vvoc surface, and silently disables new TUI features.

Remove the pin from cli.json and rely on the server plugin list for the TUI. Rejected: the client process does not read opencode.json plugins, and the host plugin dialog manages cli.json as the client plugin home.

Sync cli.json only when it already contains a managed entry, never creating one. Rejected: fresh installs would keep working only by accident of host behavior, and the incident machine would stay one bad edit away from the same drift; creating a minimal document is tolerated by the host.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Whether upgrade should additionally self-check the two pins after its sync step and fail loudly on residual mismatch is deferred; sync now repairs both pins, and doctor and status surface any manual reintroduction of drift.
Whether status should also render the cli pin for project scopes, where cli.json remains global, keeps the current single global line; no per-project behavior is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: V1-upgraded machine: cli.json holds a migrated string pin at an old version while opencode.json and the global install are current; vvoc sync rewrites the cli.json entry to the pinned specifier, preserving theme and session settings and comments; doctor afterwards prints both pins equal.
Fresh machine with no cli.json: vvoc install creates a minimal document with the cli schema URL and the plugins array carrying the pinned entry; the host loads the TUI module from it.
Manual drift: the user edits cli.json to an older pin; vvoc doctor prints the two pins and a warning naming both versions and suggesting vvoc sync; sync repairs it.
Conflicted entries: a hand-edited cli.json contains two managed vvoc entries with divergent options; the writer refuses with an explicit error and changes nothing.
Unparseable cli.json: doctor prints a bounded parse diagnostic on the TUI client pin line and continues; no command adopts a guessed pin.
